title: Enterprise security request router & priority scorecard with SLA-backed responder paths
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers submit a wide range of non-bug security & compliance requests (SOC2/ISO evidence, HIPAA attestation, GDPR/DPA clauses, and lengthy vendor questionnaires). The current intake is ad-hoc: requests land in shared inboxes, take variable time to triage, and drive inconsistent responder assignments and SLAs. Goal: build a deterministic routing + priority scorecard that classifies incoming security/compliance asks, auto-assigns the most appropriate responder queue (Security, Privacy, Legal, Solutions Eng, or CSM), and produces an SLA-backed response path and templated starter artifacts. The deliverable is a production-ready intake router specification, scoring rubric, templates, and a lightweight implementation in the onboarding workflow (Zendesk/Linear/Confluence + Slack routing).
acceptance_criteria: A1: New intake form fields collected (request type, regulatory scope, customer tier, data residency constraints, delivery urgency, estimated complexity) and validated in the form UI
A2: A deterministic priority score (0-100) computed for each submission and persisted to the ticket metadata
A3: Routing rules map score ranges and request attributes to a single responder queue; tickets are auto-assigned with correct owner 95% of test cases
A4: Each routed ticket includes a generated checklist and a templated response draft relevant to the request type
A5: SLA matrix configured (Triage within 24h for P2/above, Initial response within 48h for enterprise customers) and visible in the console/CS dashboard
A6: Instrumentation added: time-to-triage, time-to-first-response, % auto-routed, manual-reassign rate; dashboards created in Looker/Metabase
A7: Legal and Security sign-off on routing rules and templates (email thread archived)
activities: Kickoff with Security, Legal, Solutions Eng, CSMs to gather routing heuristics
Design intake form and canonical attribute schema
Define priority scorecard weights and test dataset of historical tickets
Prototype auto-routing engine (rules + fallback to manual triage) and wire in Slack alerts
Create templated response artifacts and evidence checklist per request type
Instrument and dashboard key metrics; run 2-week shadow period
Iterate rules based on shadow feedback; finalize SLA matrix; stakeholder sign-off
Roll out: update public docs and train CSM/Support rotation

risks_and_open_questions: R1: How do we handle multi-scope requests (e.g., SOC2 + HIPAA + custom DPA clauses)? Current plan is to tag primary scope and create sub-tasks for secondary scopes.
R2: SLA commitments may expose us to contractual expectations; need legal to approve explicit SLAs and fallback language.
Q1: Should the router ever auto-generate evidence exports (e.g., export of SOC2 artifacts) or only produce checklist links to where evidence lives?
Q2: For customers in APAC with stricter data residency, should routing prefer Private deployment teams?
rollout_notes: Shadow mode: 2 weeks routing suggestions surfaced to triage team (no auto-assign)
Beta: Enable auto-assign for low-risk requests from mid-market customers (2-week beta)
Full rollout: All enterprise intake flows with SLA visibility and templated responses
Training: 45-minute runbook session for Support & CSM rotation; recorded and stored in Confluence
